channel.title: Nolan Kido Living Well
channel.description: Spirituality, practical wisdom, and technology for everyday life.

item.title: What I mean by Living Well
item.description: A starting point for exploring meaning, practical wisdom, and technology without turning life into a permanent optimization project.

item.title: Can you be spiritually curious without pretending to be certain?
item.description: Keep wonder, skepticism, and personal meaning in the same conversation without forcing them to become the same thing.

item.title: What is the time you save actually for?
item.description: Before adding another automation, decide what the recovered time is meant to make possible and count the work the tool creates.

item.title: A weekly reset that does not become another job
item.description: A small paper-first review of commitments, choices, and breathing room, with an optional AI-assisted route and a clear stopping point.

item.title: Before you ask AI what to do, decide what matters
item.description: Clarify values, constraints, affected people, and uncertainty before using an AI system to examine your options.

item.title: Preserve a family story without losing the person's voice
item.description: A consent-led way to record, review, and keep a family story, with technology serving the speaker rather than replacing them.

item.title: What should you decide personally, even when a tool helps you express it?
item.description: Use help with wording without outsourcing responsibility, inventing feelings, or making promises you do not intend to keep.

item.title: The difference between improving your life and believing you are never enough
item.description: Choose a specific change without making your whole self the problem, and leave room for limits, acceptance, and outside support.

item.title: What makes an ordinary moment feel sacred?
item.description: Explore attention, ritual, wonder, and unanswered questions without claiming that a meaningful experience proves its explanation.

item.title: Can an AI-generated reflection be meaningful?
item.description: Distinguish a reader's response from the origin, accuracy, and authority of a passage, and keep AI in the role of a thinking aid.

item.title: A quiet morning does not need a dashboard
item.description: Choose one manageable boundary around attention while preserving the technology you need for care, access, work, and safety.

item.title: When does documenting your life get in the way of experiencing it?
item.description: Choose what to record, what to keep private, and when to put the camera away without treating documentation as either all good or all bad.

item.title: Plan a free afternoon without optimizing all the life out of it
item.description: Use just enough planning to support enjoyment, access, and practical constraints while leaving room for an unremarkable, worthwhile afternoon.

item.title: Make one recurring household problem less annoying
item.description: Find the smallest workable fix, use AI only where it helps, and include the people who will live with the new system.

item.title: Can a reminder help you become a more thoughtful friend?
item.description: Use technology to support remembering and showing up without turning friendship into a database or replacing the actual conversation.

item.title: Choosing between two good lives
item.description: Examine meaningful tradeoffs, test whether a plan fits ordinary days, and review disappointment without pretending every choice has one correct answer.
